answer: Here is one concrete wall: Verified ISA tenure with ISA provider attestation. It works because years the provider recorded one holder across ISAs, and the island it creates is a cost that scales with the size of the farm. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own years the provider recorded one holder across ISAs, and the ember grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. A farm could still try, but it would be paying retail for every clone while honest agents pay nothing extra; the tide is that the farm's unit economics never work.
